thread.title: Tech Today: Buffett Loves Apple, Tesla Tweet Storm, Pandora Soars

author: Barron's
title: Tech Today: Buffett Loves Apple, Tesla Tweet Storm, Pandora Soars
text:
Here are some things going on today in the world of tech :
Buffett Goes All In on Apple
Who is Apple 's ( AAPL ) biggest booster? At the moment, it is Warren Buffett . Berkshire Hathaway 's ( BRK-b ) chief executive told CNBC's Becky Quick this morning that he thinks the way the Street angsts over iPhone sales is nonsensical.
"It's an amazing business," said Buffett. "You could put all their products on a dining room table."
"The idea that you're going to spend loads of time trying to guess how many iPhone X... are going to be sold in a three-month period totally misses the point," said Buffett, according to the write-up by Berkeley Lovelace Jr.
The next part of the Quote: has to make you wonder: "It's like worrying about the number of BlackBerrys 10 years ago." Hmm.
Buffett said he bought another 75 million shares of Apple. Buffett also said Berkshire no longer holds International Business Machines ( IBM ).
Berkshire's holdings in Apple now total $43 billion , the biggest position Berkshire has ever held. As Quick noted, Berkshire is now the second-largest shareholder in Apple, behind Vanguard .
Apple stock is up $6.10, or 3.5%, at $182.99, IBM is down 64 cents at $142.63.
Defending Arista
Shares of Arista Networks ( ANET ) are down $27.91, or 10.5%, at $239.95, worsening from last night's decline after its Q1 revenue and profit beat , but the forecast for revenue this quarter was merely in line with consensus.
The worry on the conference call was that Arista's "hyperscale" customers, such as Facebook ( FB ), are all increasing their spending on equipment, while Arista seems to be decelerating.
Some price targets are being cut today, but bulls are also saying the outlook is better than people are giving credit for, given the company was up against "tough comps," as they say, from the prior-year period.
Needham & Co .'s Alex Henderson , for example, reiterates his Buy rating, and $315 price target, writing that Arista has "the best switching technology," and that it should grow 20% to 30% annually for the next three to five years.
"Investors are correctly anticipating the slowdown," after sales surged in the prior three quarters, writes Henderson. But "the demand driver news actually looks better."
Pandora Soars
Shares of the streaming-music pioneer are is up $1.15, or 20%, at $6.90, as its Q1 revenue of $319 million and a 27-cent loss per share beat the average estimate for $304 million and a 38 cent loss, as my colleague Jon Swartz reported .
The stock has gotten at least two upgrades this morning, from B. Riley and SunTrust Robinson Humphrey .
SunTrust's Matthew Thornton , raising his rating on the shares to Buy from Hold, writes that the "new leadership team is executing, communicating, and restoring much needed trust and credibility with investors."
Thornton writes there is an "inflection" here to his estimates. After many cuts to his numbers for Pandora, he's now modeling the company achieving positive Ebitda in 2019.
Elon Musk Predicts Shorts Will Be Burned
Tesla ( TSLA ) CEO Elon Musk this morning was defending his abrupt dismissal of analysts on Wednesday evening, in a quarterly conference call many called "bizarre" and "surreal," in a series of Tweets today.
Musk, referring to dismissing the question by Toni Sacconaghi of Bernstein about Tesla's capital expenditures this year, defended calling Sacconaghi's question "boneheaded" because "it had already been answered in the headline of the Q1 newsletter he received beforehand, along with details in the body of the letter."
Regarding Joseph Spak of RBC Capital 's question about how many people who've reserved a Model 3 sedan are going ahead with their purchase, Musk explained in one tweet that the question is "absurd" because Tesla has half a million reservations for Model 3s, and so "it would take two years just to satisfy demand even if new sales dropped to 0."
Musk characterized both Sacconaghi and Spak as "sell-side analysts who represent a short seller thesis, not investors." He also wrote in another tweet , "Oh and uh short burn of the century comin soon ."
Tesla shares today are up $4.57, or 1.6%, at $289.02.
Alibaba's Growth
Alibaba Group Holding (BABA) American depositary receipts are down $1.75, or 1%, at $180.70, despite beating with its Q1 revenue and earnings report this morning, reporting $9.87 billion in revenue and 91 cents per ADR in profit, versus estimates for revenue of $9.36 billion and earnings of 88 cents per ADR.
The company also forecast revenue this year well above consensus, at $63.8 billion, versus $54.5 billion expected, growing "at least 60%," the company said.
Jefferies & Co.'s Karen Chan , who has a Buy rating on the ADR, notes that the company's results show "strong" trends in its "core" commerce business, "underpinned by the largest net addition of 37 million active customers to 552 million, up 22% year-over-year."
Results were also helped by 40% growth at the company's Tmall physical retail operation. Even factoring acquisitions, the outlook for this year, writes Chan, implies 50% revenue growth.
